title: ISBLANK is TRUE only for an empty cell, returning FALSE for empty text "" (constant or formula) and for a rich picture value
statement: In Excel 16.0 builds 20430 and 20527, ISBLANK(value) returns TRUE only when value refers to a truly empty cell (or an omitted LET binding inside its body), and returns FALSE for empty text "" whether held as a cell constant or returned by a formula such as =IF(FALSE,"x",""), for all worksheet errors, and for _webimage rich values from IMAGE. On a legacy worksheet formula, a multi-cell range undergoes implicit intersection (returning FALSE when @ yields #VALUE! outside the range). Matches 1,227/1,227 full-bank and 120/120 pinned rows.
basis: Measured across Excel 16.0.20527.20196 (dc_nzpw rows 1-8, 148), Excel 16.0.20527.20088 (jnt_logical_info rows 17, 113-114; prefix_metadata row 28), Excel 16.0.20527 (fetch.rs row 518), and 1,227/1,227 full-bank and 120/120 pinned rows (ISBLANK.json).
